questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted a highly ranked university, and the University of British Columbia fit that box. I also wanted to travel to an English-speaking country as it was relevant to my degree.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I didn't have any troubles finding information I needed after I arrived in Canada.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: UBC offer a lot of support for exchange student. Both on the administrative and academic front. While I did not need these aids myself, it was comforting to know that they were there.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I didn't get the housing I applied for. However UBC did provide me with a room at Walter Gage. The facilities are not great. But most of the people who became my friends lived there and it was nice having so many exchange students and friends close by.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: The kitchen at Walter Gage was way too small for the six people it was "designed" for. As a result, I didn't use the kitchen much at all.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: If you get the opportunity, take it. Living on campus is extremely convenient. Classes were all within walking distance. Even if the facilities of the on-campus housing aren't great, the location and convenience makes it worth it.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I found the administration at UBC to be responsive and helpful - unlike what I've experienced at the University of Copenhagen. Therefore, registration was easy and I don't remember much about it as everything went smoothly.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: From my experience, whatever was needed.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got almost all the classes I applied for except one, which was already full when I applied. I also dropped a class during my exchange, which was an incredibly easy process.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
I would advise future students at UBC to really research the courses they take. Look up the profs on
ratemyprofessor.com
. Read the feedback student give. Since dropping courses is so easy at UBC, I would also advise future students to register for more courses than they plan on completing and dropping the ones they find least interesting.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: If you get a chance to take a philosophy course with Dr. Anders Kraal, take it!

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: similar or easier than what I was used to from UCPH. But the exam format is very different. All my exams were written by hand on campus.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Depends on the prof as I does at UCPH. So similar in that regard.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
PHIL375 - Philosophy and Literature
PHIL347 - Philosophy of Religion
PHIL313 - Medieval Philosophy 
CRWR205 - Introduction to Writing Creative Nonfiction

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: PHIL347 and PHIL313. Both courses were taught by Dr. Anders Kraal, which make them worth taking. I would study anything under this guy.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Groceries were extremely expensive in Vancouver.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Groceries and housing (considering the quality) were expensive.
Books were very cheap as I barely needed any for my courses.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Plenty of athletic activities. I don't know about social, as I found most of my friends on my own.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Whatever you want. There are plenty.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Spend time with your friends!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Talk the them in class!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Tipping at restaurants haha.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The welcoming attitude.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Do it!
Utilize your time there.
Make as many friends as possible.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Know that Vancouver is an expensive city.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The people I met and friends I made.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: It's not that I wasn't challenged at times during my exchange, but I learned so much about myself that I would say the biggest challenge, for me, was to not forget what I learned after my exchange - to bring those lessons home with me.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
